keyVerseText: And profited in the Jews' religion above many my equals in mine own nation, being more exceedingly zealous of the traditions of my fathers. equals: Gr. equals in years
rootMeaning: The word συνηλικιώτης (synēlikiṓtēs) is derived from the Greek prefix σύν (sýn), meaning 'with' or 'together,' combined with a derivative of ἡλικία, meaning 'age.' Thus, its root meaning conveys the idea of being 'with someone in age' or 'of the same age.' This literal sense emphasizes a close companionship or equality based on shared years, going beyond the simple English gloss of 'equals' to highlight a relational, temporal proximity among individuals.
usageInScripture: This term appears only once in Scripture, specifically in Galatians 1:14, where it is translated as 'my equals.' The singular occurrence and consistent translation underscore its precise meaning as 'those of the same age' or 'co-aged persons.' This usage reveals that Paul is emphasizing his standing among his contemporaries within his own nation, highlighting a shared generational identity that informs his zeal and religious background.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding συνηλικιώτης enriches our grasp of the relational and communal aspects of faith. It reminds believers that spiritual growth and maturity often occur within the context of peers who share similar life stages and experiences. The word's emphasis on equality in age also metaphorically points to the unity and equality found in Christ, where distinctions of background or status are secondary to the shared identity in Him. Recognizing this term's root meaning encourages believers to appreciate the fellowship among those who journey together in faith, reinforcing the biblical call to live in harmony and mutual edification within the body of Christ.
keyVerseReflection: In Galatians 1:14, Paul states, 'And profited in the Jews' religion above many my equals in mine own nation, being more exceedingly zealous of the traditions of my fathers.' The use of συνηλικιώτης here highlights that Paul was not only zealous but stood out even among his contemporaries—those who shared his cultural and generational context. This word deepens the verse's meaning by showing that Paul's zeal was exceptional not just generally, but specifically compared to those closest to him in age and background, underscoring the intensity of his early religious fervor.
